title: GitHub Outages in 2026: Why Microsoft’s Platform is Failing 100M Developers
summary:
GitHub, the backbone of modern software development with over 100 million users, is experiencing catastrophic reliability failures in 2026, with third-party monitoring reporting uptime below 86% and developers reporting daily outages blocking critical work. The platform, once hailed as a revolutionary "Facebook for code" built on Git by Linus Torvalds, now faces existential threats from unmerged pull requests, search outages, and a critical remote code execution vulnerability disclosed in April 2026. Even legendary developer Mitchell Hashimoto, creator of Vagrant and Terraform, has abandoned GitHub after documenting 30 days of outages blocking his Ghosty project, declaring the platform actively hostile to shipping software.

The core issue stems from Microsoft’s stewardship since the 2018 acquisition, where the platform’s shift toward AI-driven "agentic development workflows" has overwhelmed GitHub’s infrastructure. In April 2026 alone, GitHub’s MergeQ system unmerged 2,092 pull requests across 658 repositories, Elasticsearch was crippled by a botnet attack, and GitHub Actions faced persistent hangs. The official GitHub status page claims >99% uptime, but independent monitoring contradicts this, showing April 2026 tracking at just 86%—far below AWS S3’s "11 nines" reliability standard. The remote code execution vulnerability, where Git Push could execute code on GitHub servers, further eroded trust, prompting major projects like Zig to migrate away.
